questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that the university offered was one of the deciding factors for me choosing Sheffield.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the university sent a lot of emails regarding arrival and registration at the university as well as student support.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received emails with information on the arrival and getting to the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I had three different choices for student accommodation. All of the offers were self-catered and then I choose ensuite or to share bathroom with flatmates.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my flat we had a kitchen which I shared with my three flatmates. The university does also arrange free friday night dinners.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a great opportunity to get to know some people and for social activities in general. My accommodation was very close to the buildings I had my classes in, so I could walk there within 5-10 minutes. For this type of accommodation you need to bring or buy bedding and kitchen utensils.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an email on how to register with the university, what to bring and then I could book a time slot that suited me in the introduction week.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was staff at the registration itself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I initially applied for when I applied with the university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is an easy process when you read the emails they sent with information and look on their website where there is also information for incoming students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was similar to KU and it was as I expected. I had two year 2 courses and one year 3.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were really good and very interesting, held by professors who are specialists in their areas. We had two 50 minutes lectures for each class every week and then we had some tutorial every other week in each class (these are similar to seminars at KU, but with smaller groups around 8 people). The tutorials were really good as it was a safe space where we could discuss the content of the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took three courses: Race, Gender and Crime, Advanced EU Law, and Children and the Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend Race, Gender and Crime. It was a criminological course drawing on events and cases from society, which was really interesting and very different to anything offered at KU.

questions.answer: The cost of trip I would take while being there.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is less expensive than in DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Students' Union has a lot of different clubs and societies for both sports, academic things, culture etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join a society and do social things with others who have the same interests as yourself. I did ice skating and also some creative workshops.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend going for a walk/hike in the Peak District which is really beautiful and close to Sheffield. Otherwise, I would recommend visiting some of the other cities close to Sheffield, such as York, or to go on the day trips that the Students' Union arrange.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as I have lived in England before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would just say to be open and say yes to social activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like that it is very multi-cultural.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To be open and social and to enjoy it because time goes by so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is always good to be up to date with information and deadlines.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the good experiences, the day trips, and making friends for life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of train strikes during my exchange which sometimes made planning trips a bit difficult.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
